reason: The sampled public experience coherently expresses Precision Instrument: readable proposition, distinct client/student actions, native disclosure and station buttons, generous primary targets, skip navigation, and contrasting focus rules. Desktop/mobile hero captures support visual coherence. I traced the client journey from services and pro-bono FAQ to the contact form and its confirmation; supplied Chromium logs show that journey passing with intercepted HTTP, not actual delivery. Application source associates field errors, focuses failed fields, and accurately discloses original-resume access rather than promising anonymity. Evaluator ratings use native radios with visible peer focus. However, scoring-guide validation is less accessible, and the available local evidence cannot establish world-class accessibility across the complete authenticated workflow. This is an independent simulated expertise assessment, not observed human success.
inspected: src/app/apply/application-form.tsx (validation/focus, recovery, materials and review excerpts)

findings.evidence: RubricEditor lines 49–52 disables saving for blank names, out-of-range weights, duplicate keys and invalid key syntax. Name/weight controls lack associated explanatory errors; Key at lines 138–143 has aria-invalid only for syntax, without aria-describedby. The syntax explanation at lines 164–166 has no association, and duplicate feedback near the save control is not linked to affected inputs.
findings.userImpact: An operator navigating by fields can encounter a disabled save action without a field-level explanation of what needs correction, particularly for duplicate keys or an empty name. This is a source finding, not an observed screen-reader failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each criterion stable field/error IDs; associate specific validation guidance with aria-describedby and aria-invalid for every failing condition, including duplicates. Provide a discoverable validation summary or disabled-save explanation and verify correction using keyboard and a screen reader.

notVerified: No staging, hosted integration, actual Clerk session flow, Supabase/storage permission behavior or email delivery was observed; successful intercepted contact responses are local UI evidence only.
No screen-reader, switch/voice input, physical touch-device, Safari/Firefox, forced-colors, zoom/reflow or complete keyboard-only journey was exercised by this seat.
Private grading/operator workflows were sampled in source only; complete modal focus containment, focus restoration and all error/recovery announcements remain unverified.

Reduced-motion instrument behavior has a supplied passing Chromium assertion; global rules explicitly exempt deck-root, whose motion and operator accessibility were not assessed. No formal accessibility conformance or real-user task-success evidence exists.
